title: Conduit to the Stars
description: Extraterrestrial life has contacted our planet for the first time, through you. How do you receive their message and what is it?

title: Morning Routine
description: Pick a non-human creature. Write out their morning routine.

title: Sasquatch
description: Does Sasquatch believe? Back up your argument.

title: Horoscopes
description: Finish this sentence: Horoscopes are for ________.

title: Musical Day
description: If today existed in a musical, what are the tracks? Write out at least 5 song titles that capture the day.

title: Hand of Fate
description: Your hand is the hand of fate.

title: Terminology Ban
description: A ban has been placed on the use of all color terminology, but you are writing a description of a rainbow. How do you describe it?

title: Gum
description: What, you want more?? The prompt is 'Gum'. Good luck.

title: Echo Stream
description: A stream carries memories of all it has ever touched. Write one such memory.

title: Recipe for Posterity
description: One recipe of your creation will be passed down for generations. What is it?

title: Pen Power
description: You have a pen that imbues your words with power and influence. Describe it.

title: Kernels of Glass
description: An artist has created a larger-than-life image out of a million marbles. What's the image?

title: Mundane Superpower
description: if you could have the power to infuse magic into one boring or routine element of life, what would it be and why would you want this?

title: Roost
description: A penguin believes himself to be a rooster. What could go wrong?

title: Rewilding Playbook
description: A field manual found in the woods outlines practical steps written by future generations on how to repair fractured ecosystems. What's one key step?

title: Fifteen Generations
description: From seven generations before you to seven generations after you, everyone __________.

title: Hack the Heart
description: Write the song lyrics to the current popular hit, 'Hack the Heart'.

title: Hammer Library
description: The hammer library contains no books and no hammers. What does it hold?

title: Nurturing Homonyms
description: Tell the story of how two words that sound the same work together.

title: Rootbound
description: A groundhog named Phileene is torn between seeking her shadow and staying down under. What is the reason for her plight?

title: Sans Compass
description: Your inner toddler (i.e., inner child) has swallowed your compass. How do you get it back?

title: Monoculture
description: Pick your favorite cultural tradition. Congrats, that's now the only thing you can do from now on. Oh, and it's also the only thing everyone else can do from now on. What are the consequences?

title: Caption This
description: In the newspaper, a photograph of the newspaper which has a photograph of the newspaper on it is on the front page. What's the caption?

title: Just ad(d) water
description: Write out a commercial jingle for water. It should run no more than 20 seconds.

title: Affective Currency
description: You lose or earn money based on the emotions on your face and the stress of your environment. What expression earns you the most money when you are in line at the Department of Motor Vehicles?

title: The Coral Nest
description: Tell me a bit more about this place. Some say it's haunted.

title: Rebuilding It
description: How many times can you dismantle and rebuild the same IKEA dinner table? Provide your answer in imagery only.

title: Civic Foraging
description: You are a tour guide taking people foraging for survival skills in NYC. What borough are you in, and what items will your group learn to forage?

title: Compostable Cognitions
description: There's a new company that can compost peoples' ideas and sell the broken down components to others who need nourishing ones. You are walking down the street and see your idea in someone else's head. What is it now, and what was it in your head?

title: What I left in the womb
description: Write about what you left in the womb, why, and if you want it back.
